clue.text: Fielder taken off without reason

clue.text: Getting hooked — Snow might be concerned

definitions.note: a gerund phrase for a noun: the state of getting hooked

surface reading: the England fast bowler John Snow, whose short balls get hooked by batsmen

explanation.surface: John Snow's bouncers are being hooked for runs, and he is worried.
explanation.walkthrough: John Snow was an England fast bowler of the late 1960s and 1970s; a hook is a shot played to a short ball. Snow is also slang for cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hooked on a drug is to be dependent on it, which is the condition of being an addict.

clue.text: Maiden? There will be one in the finish

explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, so it can stand for a maiden, an old word for a girl.

clue.text: Short stop

explanation.walkthrough: A full stop ends a sentence; the two-dot mark signals a shorter pause, so it is a 'short' stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-dot punctuation mark makes a pause within a sentence, less final than a full stop.
